`CASE` works like if-else: the **first** true `WHEN` wins; with no `ELSE` the result is NULL.
```sql
SELECT c1, CASE WHEN condition1 THEN value1 WHEN condition2 THEN value2 ELSE value END AS cn FROM table_name;
```
You can use CASE in SELECT, WHERE, HAVING, ORDER BY and GROUP BY.
